events.note: Foundational education statute; actor attribution beyond promulgation remains open.
Bank of Korea Act and Banking Act promulgated in Gazette No.345.
First local council elections; political-motive interpretation must remain distinct from the fact of election implementation.
Trade Union Act and Labor Standards Act anchors; drafting and sponsorship chain remains open.
Dedicated education-finance mechanism; verify companion compulsory-education grant statute exact promulgation metadata.

adversarial_notes: Do not infer presidential personal authorship from promulgation of a statute.
Separate institutional creation of local autonomy from claims that 1952 elections were primarily a constitutional-political tactic.
Separate statutory labor protections from actual enforcement and union political control.
Separate later biographies of economic officials from contemporaneous cabinet/finance records.
Do not attribute central-bank design solely to Korean political actors without tracing US advisory and legislative drafting records.
Treat claims of educational expansion as distinct from access, quality, and fiscal-capacity outcomes.
Treat textbook regulation and political neutrality as separate institutional questions from anti-communist curricular practice.
Separate wartime inflation stabilization decisions among president, finance ministry, Bank of Korea, CEB, and UN Command.
Do not convert office-holding into responsibility for every policy adopted during the tenure.
Cross-check later developmentalist narratives against 1950s contemporaneous plans and implementation records.
